answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring a steady pulse of useful work before influence: each identity must complete small, peer-witnessed jobs week after week, building a public streak no newcomer can shortcut. That streak is the bridge to grading and payout weight, checked like light through opal, where patterns reveal whether accounts move independently. An attacker must run and pay for compute, time, and fees for every fake for months, so scaling a swarm costs real work per identity instead of a free copy.
